digest.component_or_area: documentation and architecture; reconciler backend seam
propositions: ADR 0035 contains three stale claims that the first real second backend is out of scope (diagram comment at line 111, prose at lines 204-205, Decision item 6 at lines 236-237), all falsified because epic e369 landed Jira Data Center as a second backend ahead of the reserved GitHub adapter epic be74.

The TicketTransport protocol declares six members but the reconciler calls twenty-one distinct transport methods, with twelve undeclared on any Protocol; a DC deployment crashed on set_entity_property while isinstance(backend, Backend), the contract suite, and 1636 unit tests all passed green, proving the contract suite only certifies a backend as far as the port is complete and typed.

RemoteRef.instance is presented in ADR 0035 as an existing distinction mechanism for deployments, but production code never constructs it—only test helpers do—leaving the shared-jira provenance decision partially unimplemented and undocumented.

The jira_family adapter layer introduces parameterized contracts (RichTextCodec, UserIdentityModel) and a two-level seam per vendor family; the shared jira creation channel and jira- id prefix defer generalizing jira_key and channel vocabulary to epic be74.

The DC adapter carries a deliberately time-boxed investment ending 28 March 2029 when Data Center transitions to read-only; the durable asset is the family seam architecture, not the DC-specific code, and this framing must be stated to guide future maintenance decisions.

Documentation must record that mature Jira integrations converge on maintained client libraries, PAT bearer auth, and ephemeral containerized instances as verification oracles; operational gaps (index lag, pagination caps, rate limiting, screen configuration) appear only against differently-configured instances, not in seam architecture.
